Radiator & Radiant Heat Service questions

Why is one radiator cold?

The cause can be air, a vent or trap, a closed or failed valve, poor pitch, low flow, or system imbalance. System type comes first.

Should a steam radiator valve be partly closed?

Generally no. Many one-pipe steam valves should be fully open or fully closed so condensate can return properly.

Why does the radiator bang?

Water trapped by poor pitch, high pressure, fast valves, or piping problems can create steam hammer.

Can an old radiator be replaced?

Yes when output, connection dimensions, system type, floor support, handling, and piping are planned together.

Can radiant floors be repaired without opening the floor?

Controls, pumps, manifolds, sensors, and flow can often be tested first. A tubing leak or floor defect may still require access.

Do radiator repairs need permits?

Routine repair generally does not. Replacement, new piping, boiler work, or new radiant construction may require permits depending on scope.

Which Chicago neighbourhoods do you cover?

Chicago citywide, plus the near north and northwest suburbs. Ask us for our current municipal registrations before you book anything outside the city - we will give you the list rather than a marketing map.

My building is a pre-war two-flat. Does that change the job?

Usually yes. West Chicago township, covering Wicker Park and West Town, is 83.0% pre-1940. In stock that age the masonry flue and the lack of duct routes are the variables that decide the price.

Do you work in condo buildings?

Yes, though associations frequently have their own rules on venting, roof access and shutoffs. Get those requirements in writing before you book anyone.

Chicago heating & cooling library

Chicago housing stock

Cook County Assessor data for the eight townships covering Chicago records 439,398 assessed properties: 305,736 single-family and 133,662 multi-family. The same service can mean a basement system in a bungalow, shared equipment in a two-flat, or roof and association access in a condo building.

335,769 properties use warm-air furnaces and 98,849 use hot-water or steam heat. 324,305 have full basements. Access, distribution, shared flues, old piping, electrical capacity and decades of alterations can change scope before equipment brand does.

What actually needs a permit

Chicago issued 62,810 permits of all types in the 24 months to August 2026. 4,888 mention HVAC work, while 7,993 carry a ventilation, refrigeration or heating trade contractor contact.

Repair, diagnosis and routine maintenance generally do not require a construction permit. New equipment, altered systems, exterior penetrations, fuel work and electrical work may. The proposal should name the responsible permit holder and any second trade.

sections.html:
Radiator & Radiant Heat Service questions

Why is one radiator cold?

The cause can be air, a vent or trap, a closed or failed valve, poor pitch, low flow, or system imbalance. System type comes first.

Should a steam radiator valve be partly closed?

Generally no. Many one-pipe steam valves should be fully open or fully closed so condensate can return properly.

Why does the radiator bang?

Water trapped by poor pitch, high pressure, fast valves, or piping problems can create steam hammer.

Can an old radiator be replaced?

Yes when output, connection dimensions, system type, floor support, handling, and piping are planned together.

Can radiant floors be repaired without opening the floor?

Controls, pumps, manifolds, sensors, and flow can often be tested first. A tubing leak or floor defect may still require access.

Do radiator repairs need permits?

Routine repair generally does not. Replacement, new piping, boiler work, or new radiant construction may require permits depending on scope.

Which Chicago neighbourhoods do you cover?

Chicago citywide, plus the near north and northwest suburbs. Ask us for our current municipal registrations before you book anything outside the city - we will give you the list rather than a marketing map.

My building is a pre-war two-flat. Does that change the job?

Usually yes. West Chicago township, covering Wicker Park and West Town, is 83.0% pre-1940. In stock that age the masonry flue and the lack of duct routes are the variables that decide the price.

Do you work in condo buildings?

Yes, though associations frequently have their own rules on venting, roof access and shutoffs. Get those requirements in writing before you book anyone.

sections.html:
Chicago heating & cooling library

Chicago housing stock

Cook County Assessor data for the eight townships covering Chicago records 439,398 assessed properties: 305,736 single-family and 133,662 multi-family. The same service can mean a basement system in a bungalow, shared equipment in a two-flat, or roof and association access in a condo building.

335,769 properties use warm-air furnaces and 98,849 use hot-water or steam heat. 324,305 have full basements. Access, distribution, shared flues, old piping, electrical capacity and decades of alterations can change scope before equipment brand does.

What actually needs a permit

Chicago issued 62,810 permits of all types in the 24 months to August 2026. 4,888 mention HVAC work, while 7,993 carry a ventilation, refrigeration or heating trade contractor contact.

Repair, diagnosis and routine maintenance generally do not require a construction permit. New equipment, altered systems, exterior penetrations, fuel work and electrical work may. The proposal should name the responsible permit holder and any second trade.

Where we work

This content set publishes Chicago only. It uses one shared area document so the system does not create duplicate neighbourhood pages or imply unverified suburban registrations.

Within Chicago, condo rules, roof access, tenant or owner approval, shared utilities, working hours and parking can still change scheduling and scope.

Evidence for radiator and radiant heat repair and installation

The city source classifies 98 radiant/radiator permits tagged, 24mo. That count is used only to explain the available evidence; it is not represented as City & Suburban’s work.

The sample is not used as a consumer price benchmark. The page instead identifies the equipment, access, controls, connections, responsible trade, inspection or testing, and permit status that belong in a written quote.

Scope flags in the source workbook remain visible in Sanity so an editor can verify adjacent, low-volume, confirmation-required, or out-of-scope services before publication.
